name: Zeleciment Rostudirsen (DYNE-251)
summary: Z-rostudirsen (DYNE-251) is Dyne's Fab-conjugated PMO that skips exon 51 of the dystrophin gene, dosed IV at 20 mg/kg every four weeks. The BLA, built on the registrational expansion cohort of the Phase 1/2 DELIVER trial (NCT05524883, dystrophin at 6 months), seeks accelerated approval for DMD amenable to exon 51 skipping; FDA granted Priority Review with a PDUFA date of 2027-01-21, and FORZETTO (NCT07608432, ambulatory ages 4 to 18, rise-from-floor velocity at week 73, primary completion 2030-12) is the confirmatory Phase 3. Price anchor: Exondys 51 (eteplirsen), the marketed exon 51 skipper, at its $16/mg WAC, $748,800 a year for ICER's 30 kg reference patient, less Sarepta's filed 18.5% gross-to-net; the book holds no CMS rows for Exondys. Pool: the book's DMD figures (11,952 prevalent, 367 a year) restricted to the 13% amenable to exon 51 skipping. Uptake anchor: Exondys's own revenue, converted to US patient-equivalents at this net price, reached 42% of the exon 51 pool in its fifth year (2021); the engine needs a 0.0953 annual capture on a step-shaped ramp to match that.

therapy_mode.source: Dyne 10-Q for Q2 2026 (0001193125-26-323639, MD&A): FORZETTO randomises to 20 mg/kg z-rostudirsen or placebo every four weeks (Q4W) IV; Dyne JPM 2026 deck (8-K 0001193125-26-009782, EX-99): registrational dose 20 mg/kg Q4W
therapy_mode.note: Continuous dosing every four weeks, not a single course
therapy_mode.check: Context file: NCT07608432 (Phase 3, Recruiting, Dyne lead sponsor) is titled 'Zeleciment Rostudirsen (DYNE-251) Administered Intravenously Every 4 Weeks'; the BLA acceptance coverage (NeurologyLive, CureDuchenne, Dyne release, search) describes a continuing treatment seeking accelerated approval, not a single course. Chronic is right. The 10-Q and JPM deck accessions were not opened (sec.gov is blocked from this container).

list_price_per_patient.source: ICER, 'Deflazacort, Eteplirsen, and Golodirsen for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy' (2019; icer.org/assessment/duchenne-muscular-dystrophy-2019/ and the modeling analysis plan, icer.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/ICER_DMD_Modeling_Analysis_Plan_040919.pdf): eteplirsen WAC $16 per mg, $748,800 a year for a 30 kg patient at the label dose of 30 mg/kg weekly (16 x 30 x 30 x 52 = 748,800). Vial prices at launch: $1,600 per 100 mg (2 mL) and $8,000 per 500 mg (10 mL) (BioPharma Dive, 'Sarepta names that price', biopharmadive.com/news/sarepta-price-eteplirsen-dmd/426636/)
list_price_per_patient.note: JUDGEMENT on the comparator and the reference weight. The caller asked for Exondys via lookup.py demand, but the book holds no drug_demand row for Exondys 51, Vyondys 53, Amondys 45 or Elevidys (checked by brand name and by asset_id 107), data.cms.gov is blocked from this container (403), and two searches did not surface its CMS Part B figure. A published WAC beats the CMS convention in any case. Exondys is the only marketed exon 51 skipper and z-rostudirsen seeks the same label, so it is priced at parity. Case for higher: price is weight-based and EVOLVE's commercial eteplirsen patients averaged 14.0 years of age, heavier than 30 kg (at 45 kg the same WAC gives $1,123,200); the $16/mg WAC dates from 2019 and later increases were not checked; Dyne may ask a premium for monthly rather than weekly infusions and higher dystrophin. Case for lower: DELIVER enrolled ages 4 to 16 and a 20 kg boy costs $499,200; Sarepta's own launch statement put the average near $300,000 a year (BioPharma Dive, as above); payers may resist a second accelerated approval in the same exon.
list_price_per_patient.check: BioPharma Dive 'Sarepta names that price' (search): a 2 mL vial costs $1,600 and a 10 mL vial $8,000; at 50 mg/mL that is 100 mg and 500 mg, so $16/mg. Label dose 30 mg/kg once weekly (same search). Recomputed 16 x 30 mg/kg x 30 kg x 52 = $748,800 = 0.7488 mm USD per patient-year; unit right. Drugs.com (search) shows about $1,571 cash for 2 mL today, so no large WAC increase since launch is visible. Not seen: the ICER page or modelling plan stating the 30 kg reference patient (the JMCP summary of ICER's 2019 review, PMID 32223600, has no full text in PMC), so the 30 kg rests on the researcher's citation; the weight is labelled a judgement with its case both ways. Book: drug_demand holds 0 rows for Exondys, Vyondys or Amondys (asset id 107 exists, no CMS rows), so the WAC route is the only one. Wording caveat in the note: the same BioPharma Dive piece gives Sarepta's $300,000 as the 'expected net annual cost for a 25 kg boy, taking into account changes in weight-based dosing over time and expected compliance', not a plain average; against a 25 kg list of $624,000 that is 48% of list. The model handles this only because penetration is solved in revenue-parity patient-equivalents at this same price (see penetration_peak_pct).

gross_to_net_pct.source: Sarepta FY2024 10-K (0000950170-25-029973), Note 7 reserves table: FY2023 provision for chargebacks, rebates, prompt pay and other accruals $258,646k, prior-year adjustments -$4,567k, net product revenue $1,144,876k. Gross = 1,144,876 + 258,646 - 4,567 = 1,398,955; 258,646 / 1,398,955 = 0.1849
gross_to_net_pct.note: Direction checked: share off list, so net is $610,358 a patient-year. Anchor is a WAC, so neither house convention applies; the discount is Sarepta's own filed one. FY2023 is used because PMOs were 82.5% of product revenue that year ($944.5mm of $1,144.9mm). FY2024 gives 0.1842 (same table); FY2025 gives 0.2140 (FY2025 10-K 0001193125-26-084144), lifted by PHS chargebacks after Elevidys lost its pediatric designation. Case against: the figure blends in Elevidys; a new entrant may concede larger rebates to win formulary position against Exondys.
gross_to_net_pct.check: Sarepta FY2023 10-K (0000950170-24-022036, search): 2023 provision for current-period sales $258,646k = chargebacks 44,191 + rebates 129,724 + prompt pay 15,067 + other accruals 69,664 (sums exactly). Recomputed 258,646 / (1,144,876 + 258,646 - 4,567) = 0.18489; without the -4,567 prior-year adjustment (not seen by me) 258,646 / 1,403,522 = 0.1843, so the value holds either way. Direction right: share off list, net = 0.7488 x (1 - 0.184885) = $610,358. A WAC anchor, so neither the 0.5 Part D nor the 0.056604 Part B convention applies; the discount is sourced from the comparator's own filing. The blend with Elevidys and ex-US sales is stated in the note as the case against.

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of the treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: EVOLVE, Phase 4 US observational study of commercial PMOs (Tian C et al., J Comp Eff Res 2026;15(5):e250108, doi:10.57264/cer-2025-0108, PMID 41961051; NCT06606340): 120 of 126 eteplirsen patients (95.2%) continued treatment over a mean 6.2 years on therapy; 34 of 37 who lost ambulation stayed on eteplirsen. 1 - (120/126)^(1/6.2) = 0.0078
discontinuation_pct.note: Constant hazard from the continuation share. JUDGEMENT that it transfers: EVOLVE is Sarepta-sponsored and enrolled patients already on therapy, so it is a survivor cohort and a floor; deaths (DMD life expectancy near 30 years) and switches to Elevidys are not in it. Case for higher: Exondys's revenue flattened after 2021 (US PMO revenue $797.9mm 2023, $816.9mm 2024, $800.4mm 2025, with Vyondys and Amondys growing inside it), and the engine only reproduces that plateau with 15-20% a year; at 0.0078 the treated stock keeps accumulating. Case for lower: none measured
discontinuation_pct.check: PubMed PMID 41961051 (Tian C et al., J Comp Eff Res 2026;15(5):e250108, doi:10.57264/cer-2025-0108, NCT06606340) abstract: 126 eteplirsen patients, mean total treatment 6.2 years, 95.2% (n=120) continued; 37 of 85 ambulatory at start lost ambulation and 34 (91.9%) stayed on eteplirsen. Recomputed 1 - (120/126)^(1/6.2) = 0.00784. Labelled a judgement with its case against (Sarepta-sponsored survivor cohort of prevalent users, no deaths). My run of the engine agrees the concern is real: with 0.0078 and no mortality the treated stock keeps rising (1,279 by year 12, 82% of the US exon 51 pool) while Exondys revenue flattened after 2021. Inputs confirmed and the judgement is disclosed, so confirmed; the build should read the tail with this in mind.

forecast_start_year.source: Dyne 8-K 2026-07-20 (0001193125-26-308343): BLA accepted with Priority Review, PDUFA target action date 2027-01-21, 'potential U.S. launch of z-rostudirsen in the first quarter of 2027'; repeated in the Q2 2026 release (8-K 0001193125-26-323940)
forecast_start_year.note: The first full year after the current one, and the launch year. The confirmatory FORZETTO primary completion (2030-12) does not gate accelerated approval. The ramp below allows for 2027 being a launch year
forecast_start_year.check: Search (Dyne release 2026-07-20 via GlobeNewswire/BioSpace, NeurologyLive, Practical Neurology, CureDuchenne): FDA accepted the z-rostudirsen BLA for DMD amenable to exon 51 skipping, seeking Accelerated Approval on dystrophin, Priority Review, PDUFA target action date January 21, 2027; Dyne 'continues to expect a potential U.S. launch of z-rostudirsen in Q1 2027'. 2027 is the first full year after 2026 and the launch year. Context file: FORZETTO NCT07608432 primary completion 2030-12, confirmatory, so it does not gate launch.

exus_multiple.source: Sarepta FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-084144), Note 7: PMO Products net revenue United States $800,382k, Rest of World $165,183k in 2025; 165,183 / 800,382 = 0.2064
exus_multiple.note: JUDGEMENT on the comparator: the PMOs (Exondys, Vyondys, Amondys) are the only filed geographic split for exon-skipping drugs. The ratio was 0.184 in 2024 and 2023 and 0.129 in 2022 (FY2024 10-K 0000950170-25-029973). Sarepta's ex-US sales come through distributors in South America, Europe and the Middle East without an EU approval: the book's EMA register lists Exondys (eteplirsen, EMEA/H/C/004355) as Refused, and golodirsen and casimersen are absent. Case for higher: Dyne says it 'continues to pursue approval pathways outside of the U.S.' (8-K 0001193125-26-323940) and puts the EU DMD population at about 16,000 against 12,000 in the US (8-K 0001193125-26-009782); an EU approval would lift this. Case for lower: Dyne has no ex-US commercial partner or infrastructure on file
exus_multiple.check: Sarepta FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-084144, search): PMO products net revenue United States $800,382k, Rest of World $165,183k in 2025 (total $965,565k). Recomputed 165,183 / 800,382 = 0.2064. 2022 ratio implied by the researcher's US share (747.1 of 843.8) is 0.1294, matching the note. Book check: the engine (backend/forecast.py) multiplies both the pool and the inflow by 1 + exus_multiple, and the identity is linear in pool size, so the penetration solved on the US pool still reproduces the US revenue and adds 20.6% ex-US. Labelled a judgement (no EU approval for any exon-skipper; Dyne has no ex-US partner) with cases both ways.

economics_share.source: Dyne FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-084178, patents section): Dyne owns its DMD patent estate (29 issued US patents, expiring 2039 and 2042); the only in-licence, from the University of Mons, covers oligonucleotides for the FSHD programme; the December 2025 Avidity cross-licence is 'royalty-free, fully paid up, non-exclusive'
economics_share.note: No partner, royalty or profit share on z-rostudirsen found in the 10-K, the Q2 2026 10-Q (0001193125-26-323639) or the 2026 8-Ks
economics_share.check: Not reopened at the filing level (sec.gov blocked, search allowance spent on price and uptake). What I saw: Dyne is the lead sponsor of both z-rostudirsen trials (context file), is the sole BLA applicant, and plans its own US launch in Q1 2027 (BLA release, search); no partner, co-promote or royalty on z-rostudirsen appeared in any result. 1.0 is the brief's default for an unpartnered asset. The Avidity cross-licence and Mons in-licence terms rest on the researcher's 10-K citation.

prevalence.source: carried by the book: the deramiocel (CAPR) seed's figure, /tmp/claude-0/price/out/CAPR_deramiocel_cap_1002.json: Crisafulli S et al., Orphanet J Rare Dis 2020;15:141 (PMID 32503598, doi:10.1186/s13023-020-01430-8), 7.1 per 100,000 males, applied to 168.34mm US males (Census Bureau Vintage 2024)
prevalence.note: Carried by the book: the same figure as the deramiocel seed so one disease keeps one number, written out rather than null so it does not depend on the order seeds load. Independent check agrees: Dyne's JPM 2026 deck puts US DMD at about 12,000 (8-K 0001193125-26-009782), 0.4% away. Any correction should be settled for both assets together
prevalence.check: Same figure as the deramiocel seed (out/CAPR_deramiocel_cap_1002.json: 11,952), so the disease keeps one number. PubMed PMID 32503598 (Crisafulli 2020, doi:10.1186/s13023-020-01430-8) abstract: pooled prevalence 7.1 per 100,000 males (95% CI 5.0-10.1). Recomputed 168.34mm x 7.1 / 100,000 = 11,952. The 168.34mm US males was not independently opened. Wording caveat: lookup.py pool 'Duchenne' and 'Muscular Dystrophy, Duchenne' return nothing and epidemiology.csv has no DMD row, so book.db does not yet carry it; it is carried by the CAPR seed (itself not yet second-read), and writing it out rather than null is right. Dyne's own ~12,000 US cross-check is in the researcher's JPM citation.

incidence.source: carried by the book: the deramiocel (CAPR) seed's figure: Crisafulli 2020 birth prevalence 19.8 per 100,000 live male births x 1,854,394 US male births in 2024 (3,628,934 births, NVSR Births: Final Data for 2024)
incidence.note: Carried by the book, same figure as the deramiocel seed. The engine passes it through eligible_pct: 367 x 0.13 = 48 exon 51-amenable boys a year
incidence.check: Matches the deramiocel seed (367). Crisafulli 2020 (PMID 32503598) abstract: birth prevalence 19.8 per 100,000 live male births. 3,628,934 US births in 2024 is the NVSR figure already confirmed by the GSK MMRV and varicella second reads (verified/GSK_mmrvns_vaccine.json). Recomputed 3,628,934 x 1,045/2,045 = 1,854,394 male births x 19.8e-5 = 367.2. The engine filters it by eligible_pct: 367 x 0.13 = 47.7 a year.

eligible_pct.source: Aartsma-Rus A et al., 'Theoretic applicability of antisense-mediated exon skipping for Duchenne muscular dystrophy mutations', Hum Mutat 2009;30:293-9 (PMID 19156838, doi:10.1002/humu.20918), Leiden DMD mutation database: 'Exon 51 skipping ... would be applicable to the largest group (13%) of all DMD patients'. Dyne cites the same 13% (8-K 0001193125-26-009782). BLA population: 'individuals with ... DMD amenable to exon 51 skipping' (8-K 0001193125-26-308343)
eligible_pct.note: How the pool is restricted: the book's all-DMD prevalence and incidence are multiplied by the 13% whose mutation is amenable to exon 51 skipping, 11,952 x 0.13 = 1,554 US patients plus 48 a year. That is the only filter. No age or ambulatory filter is applied, because the BLA asks for the whole exon 51-amenable population (Exondys's label has neither restriction) and DELIVER enrolled both ambulant and non-ambulant boys aged 4 to 16 (8-K 0001193125-26-009782). JUDGEMENT that the label follows the BLA. Case for lower: FDA could restrict an accelerated approval to DELIVER's ages or to ambulatory patients (FORZETTO is ambulatory only, ages 4 to 18), and only genetically confirmed patients are addressable. The 13% comes from a 2009 database; the TREAT-NMD database (Bladen CL et al., Hum Mutat 2015, PMID 25604253) reports exon-skipping applicability overall, not by exon, in its abstract
eligible_pct.check: PubMed PMID 19156838 (Aartsma-Rus A et al., Hum Mutat 2009;30:293-9, doi:10.1002/humu.20918) abstract: 'Exon 51 skipping ... would be applicable to the largest group (13%) of all DMD patients' (Leiden DMD database). The deramiocel seed cites the same 13% for exon 51 from Sarepta's 10-K risk factors. BLA population is DMD amenable to exon 51 skipping (search), and the engine applies it to both pool and inflow, so the pool is the label's: 11,952 x 0.13 = 1,553.8 plus 47.7 a year. No age or ambulatory filter, labelled a judgement with the case for a narrower accelerated-approval label.

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the eligible untreated pool captured per year
penetration_peak_pct.source: Exondys 51 net revenue $154.6mm 2017 (Sarepta FY2017 results release, investorrelations.sarepta.com), $380.7mm 2019, $422.0mm 2020, $454.4mm 2021 (Sarepta FY2021 10-K, sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/873303/000095017022002517/srpt-20211231.htm). Converted to US patient-equivalents at this seed's net price ($610,358): x 0.8854 US share (PMO US $747.1mm of $843.8mm in 2022, FY2024 10-K 0000950170-25-029973) / 0.6104 = 224 (2017), 552 (2019), 612 (2020), 659 (2021). Over the US exon 51 pool of 1,554, Exondys held 14% in its first full year and 42% in its fifth (2021). The engine (pool 1,554, inflow 48 a year, the untreated pool held stationary at 0.9702, discontinuation 0.0078, ramp below) needs 0.1016 to reach 659 in year five (0.0953 with no retention set)
penetration_peak_pct.note: MEASURED: Exondys's own capture of the untreated exon 51 pool, applied as it was measured, with no multiple. It is a revenue-parity figure: patient-equivalents at the model's own price, so the model reproduces Exondys's revenue at the same age of launch whatever the true average weight. Exondys's 659 US patient-equivalents (2021) are out of the pool this seed draws on (already_treated_patients), so z-rostudirsen captures at the incumbent's measured rate from the untreated remainder rather than replaying Exondys's launch into all 1,554. The 2018 figure was not confirmed ($295-305mm guidance only) and is left out; the US share for 2017 to 2021 is the 2022 PMO share, a judgement. Case for higher: monthly rather than weekly infusions and higher dystrophin expression, and Exondys patients can switch, which the netting does not allow. Case for lower: Elevidys competes for ambulatory patients aged 4 and over, and at 0.78% discontinuation the stock keeps accumulating on the untreated remainder (see discontinuation_pct)
penetration_peak_pct.check: defect review 2026-09-25: Exondys's capture re-solved under the stationary pool, applied without a multiple, on the pool net of Exondys's patients; was 0.0953 (confirmed)

ramp_steepness.source: Least-squares fit (log errors) of the engine's curve to the four Exondys patient-equivalent points above (224, 552, 612, 659 in years 0, 2, 3, 4 from 2017), with discontinuation 0.0078
ramp_steepness.note: Measured from the closest comparator; the book has no modelled DMD seed to reuse. The fit is a step: Exondys reached its full capture rate in its first full year, and any k of 4 or more with a midpoint of -1 or earlier fits alike (a free fit settles at k 4.0, midpoint -2.0, peak 0.12, but overshoots 2021 by 20%). At k 4.0 and midpoint -1.0 the curve gives 98% of peak in year 0. Case against: 2027 is Dyne's launch year (approval 2027-01-21), while 2017 was Exondys's first full year after a September 2016 approval; at this peak the curve undershoots Exondys's early years (150 against 224 in year 0, 423 against 552 in year 2), which partly offsets that
ramp_steepness.check: Refit by grid search on log errors to the four patient-equivalent points (years 0, 2, 3, 4) with discontinuation 0.0078: the unconstrained best is a step (k 8, midpoint -4, peak 0.12, log-SSE 0.068) that overshoots 2021 by 20% (794 against 659), matching the researcher's description; any k of 4 or more with midpoint of -2 or earlier is flat. At k 4.0, midpoint -1.0 and peak 0.0953 the log-SSE is 0.247 and year 0 runs at 98.2% of peak (1/(1+e^-4)). Undershoots 2017 (150 against 224) and 2019 (423 against 552), as stated. Measured from the only exon 51 comparator; the launch-year versus first-full-year offset (Exondys approved September 2016, Dyne PDUFA 2027-01-21) is disclosed.

ramp_midpoint_year.source: as ramp_steepness (fit to Exondys 51's revenue-implied US patients)
ramp_midpoint_year.note: A negative midpoint puts the inflection before the first forecast year, which is what a step-shaped launch looks like on this curve. JUDGEMENT to hold -1.0 rather than the free fit's -2.0; the two are near-identical in year 0 (98% against 99.97% of peak). A midpoint of 0.0 would need a peak of 0.1047 to match 2021 and fits the early years four times worse
ramp_midpoint_year.check: Same refit: midpoint -1.0 gives 98.2% of peak in year 0 against 99.97% at -2.0. A midpoint of 0.0 needs a peak of 0.1047 to hit 659 in year 4 and gives log-SSE 1.10, 4.5 times the -1.0 fit (researcher says four times). Negative midpoint is legitimate in the engine (s_curve uses it as an offset from the first forecast year). Labelled a judgement with its case against.

already_treated_patients.source: Exondys 51's US patient-equivalents in 2021, the last year Sarepta reported it apart from its other PMOs (it reports them together from 2022): $454.4mm net revenue (Sarepta FY2021 10-K, sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/873303/000095017022002517/srpt-20211231.htm) x 0.8854 US share / this seed's $610,358 net price = 659, the same series penetration_peak_pct is solved from
already_treated_patients.note: The incumbent's measured patients, taken out of the untreated pool the engine draws on. Case for more: Exondys kept growing after 2021 inside Sarepta's PMO line, so more boys may be on it by the 2027 launch. Case for fewer: some of these are patient-equivalents rather than boys, since heavier patients take more drug
already_treated_patients.check: defect review 2026-09-25: the incumbent's measured patients leave the opening pool

untreated_carryover_pct.source: retention = pool / (pool + inflow) = 1,553.76 / (1,553.76 + 47.71) = 0.9702, the brief's rule for a chronic disease whose pool would otherwise outgrow its measured prevalence, as the remternetug and direclidine seeds do; the SGT-003 seed holds the same Duchenne pool at 0.9702
untreated_carryover_pct.note: JUDGEMENT, the house rule. The engine has no death term, so at the default 1.0 the untreated pool grew by 48 boys a year for ever. Penetration is re-solved from Exondys under the same retention, so the capture stays the measured one
untreated_carryover_pct.check: defect review 2026-09-25: the house rule's stationary pool, flagged missing by the second reader
